details: Escalating tensions between the United States and Iran, fueled by Houthi attacks in the Red Sea and threats of a strong US response, have led to a decline in Bitcoin's price. Bitcoin fell below $65,000 to a three-day low on July 24, with some reports indicating it briefly slipped below $64,000. This geopolitical uncertainty, coupled with rising Brent crude oil prices surpassing $100 per barrel and renewed inflation fears, has spurred risk aversion in markets. Additionally, Bitcoin Spot ETFs experienced significant outflows, with $225.2 million in net outflows on July 23, breaking a seven-day positive streak. Over $312 million in total crypto liquidations were triggered as Bitcoin's price dropped.
title: US-Iran Tensions Drive Bitcoin Decline Amid ETF Outflows

details: The European Union adopted its 21st package of sanctions against Russia on July 23, directly targeting financial services and cryptocurrencies to further cripple Russia's war economy. The new measures include transaction bans on 14 crypto-related service platforms operating across six jurisdictions: Georgia, Panama, the UAE, the Marshall Islands, Kyrgyzstan, and Belarus. For the first time, the EU has introduced a mechanism allowing for a full third-country ban on crypto-asset services, enabling regulators to prohibit transactions with entire jurisdictions hosting platforms that aid Russia in evading EU sanctions.
title: EU Imposes 21st Sanctions Package on Russia, Targets Crypto Services
